pr.body:
Supersedes #504. Since d90c086 (#505) a regex literal is recognized before
strings, which fixes most of what #504 addressed: of its 23 tests, 20 pass on
`master`. This PR keeps only what is still missing, in the style of
d90c086, rebased on `master` after 1.24.3 (01afe9c).

### The problem

A regex literal is recognized only after expression-opening punctuation
(`=,({[?:!&|;`), not after `=>` or after a keyword such as `return`:

```js
function a(s) {
  return /#/.test(s) || s === 1;
}

function b(list) {
  return list.filter(s => /"/.test(s) || s === "a");
}

function c(s) {
  return s;
}
```

```
$ lizard r.js          # master, 01afe9c
       3      1      8      1       3 a@1-3@r.js
       1      1      5      0       1 (anonymous)@6-6@r.js
       3      1     14      1       3 b@5-7@r.js
       3      1      8      1       3 c@9-11@r.js
```

In `a`, `#` starts a preprocessor line and the `||` is lost; in the arrow
function of `b`, the quote opens a string. Both should have a cyclomatic
complexity of 2.

### What changes

`REGEX_TOKEN` in `js_style_regex_expression.py` also accepts a literal after
`=>` and after the keywords after which an expression starts (`return`,
`typeof`, `instanceof`, `in`, `of`, `new`, `delete`, `void`, `throw`,
`case`, `do`, `else`, `yield`, `await`). With the fix:

```
       3      2     17      1       3 a@1-3@r.js
       1      2     11      0       1 (anonymous)@6-6@r.js
       3      1     14      1       3 b@5-7@r.js
       3      1      8      1       3 c@9-11@r.js
```

### How it is tested

Tokenizer tests in `test/test_languages/testJavaScript.py`, function-end
tests in `test/test_languages/testJavaScriptRegex.py` (`#`, `[?#]`, `\/`,
quotes, backticks, braces, character classes and flags, in `.js`, `.ts`,
`.jsx` and `.tsx`) and two tests in `test/testNestedStructures.py` (nesting
after a regex literal, in the same file and in the next file). The three
tests on `return` and `=>` fail on `master`; the others pass there and are
kept as guards. The full suite passes on the branch: `python -m pytest test`
gives 1688 passed, 7 skipped (1665 passed on `master`).

### What does not change

Division (`a / b / c`, `(a) / b / c`, `a[0]/b/c`) and the other tokens. The
Ruby reader uses the same decorator, so `return /#/ =~ s ? 1 : 0` now gives
a complexity of 2 there too, where `#` used to start a comment;
`s.split(/,/)` and `s.gsub(/[\/"]/, "")` are unchanged.

Thank you warmly for the fix in d90c086: recognizing the literal before the
strings is a cleaner solution than the one I had proposed, and it made this
PR much smaller. More generally, thank you for all the work you put into
lizard and for the attention you give to every report.
pr.title: Recognize a JavaScript/TypeScript regex literal after "=>" and keywords
